newsitem.title: USA: New Hampshire plane crash caused by carbon monoxide.
newsitem.headline: New Hampshire plane crash caused by carbon monoxide.

text.p: Two pilots killed when their small plane crashed after they lost consciousness in the skies over New England suffered from carbon monoxide poisoning, authorities said on Tuesday.

David Riach, 46, of Babylon, New York, and his mother Dorothy Riach, 71, of Morristown, New Jersey, died from of a combination of carbon monoxide poisoning and injuries suffered when their plane crashed, Kathy Descheneaux of the New Hampshire Medical Examiner's office said.

Authorities believe carbon monoxide fumes leaked into the cabin of the single-engine Piper Cherokee and caused David Riach to pass out as his plane was enroute on Friday from Farmingdale, New York, to Saranack Lake, New York.

Dorothy Riach, who had more limited flying experience, radioed authorities about her son's condition but apparently blacked out before she could try to land the aircraft at an airport in southern Connecticut.

"We found a hole in the muffler," said Beverley Drake-Nurse, lead investigator in the crash from the National Transportation Safety Board in Washington. The cabins of some small planes are heated by pumping air from the warm engine and a leaky muffler could cause carbon monoxide to be passed into the passenger compartment, she said.

After the elder Riach passed out, the four-seat plane continued to fly on autopilot, passing over three states before it ran out of fuel and crashed in a densely wooded area of Alton, a rural community in central New Hampshire.
